title: Cryogenic etching for 3D NAND
summary: Etching memory holes at very low temperature to reach higher layer counts.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Cryogenic etch cools the wafer far below room temperature during deep reactive-ion etching, improving profile control and throughput for the high-aspect-ratio channels in 3D NAND. Tokyo Electron has positioned the technique as a route to more than 400 layers, where conventional etch struggles to reach the bottom uniformly. The approach matters because NAND scaling now happens vertically, not laterally.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Early commercial
Estimated window 2024–2028
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

NAND density is an etch and deposition problem as much as a lithography one, which shifts value to back-end toolmakers.

What Would Change The View

  • Adoption at major NAND makers.
  • Cost per wafer versus conventional etch.
  • Equipment throughput in production.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
